K1001.phase: Largest-Δ (≥3× gap) win rate depends on the smaller Δ: <0.03 ~95% (tabular lab 2011/2135); 0.03-0.1 ~60-88%; once smaller Δ≥0.1 only 25-60% (bigram 25%, tabular 43%, spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58%, univariate 60%; K1012, K1021). LR-ceiling breaks: K1004.

K1004.mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).
K1004.phase: RMSprop≥3e-3 vs ≥3× smaller-Δ choice on MSE: RMSprop net has higher LN+residual score → wins 6/6; equal → 12/22; lower → 4/8. RMSprop 1e-3 univariate 1/4.

regime.note: (a) corpus regression pairs; (b) bigram post-LN transformer vs GRU

K1006.mechanism: Each unnormalized pre-activation layer shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU at init), so an under-trained deep stack feeds a weak signal to the head; pre-LN restores unit scale and identity paths keep gradient flow, speeding an under-trained net 2-3x. Predicts the LN advantage shrinks once Δ is large enough to learn the scale (tabular Δ>=0.1 reverses, K1009) and where LN destroys label-relevant norm information (2-D spiral, K1020).
K1006.phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12, tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); spiral plain+LN vs residual: residual 7/9 (K1020); XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10 (weak).

regime.note: tabular only when Δ<0.1; spiral handled by K1020; same optimizer/lr/T

K1008.mechanism: SiLU/GELU have derivative ≈0.5 at 0 and sub-unit gain over typical pre-activations, so each un-normalized block shrinks signal and gradient (≈0.5^depth), slowing fitting in an under-trained regime; ReLU-family keep gain ~1 on the active side. Predicts the SiLU penalty shrinks when every block has LN (re-scales) and grows with depth of unnormalized stacks; on classification with distractors the smooth curvature regularizes confidence instead, flipping the sign (K1009/K1018).

regime.note: corpus same-optimizer pairs; activation pairs often confounded with depth/LN

K1009.mechanism: With 1024 rows and labels set by 2-4 coordinates, once Δ≥0.1 the decision boundary is already fit; test CE is then set by logit scale on misclassified points, so anything that speeds fitting (depth, LN, ReLU kinks, larger lr) inflates confidence. Predicts the same reversal for optimizer Δ (K1021) and no reversal on XOR/spiral where the boundary is still being learned.
K1009.phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ per core rule

K1011.phase: GRU-vs-post-LN-TF same optimizer: corpus GRU 20/21; Δ<0.01 GRU 8/10 (lab+corpus); 0.02-0.05 GRU 2/2 corpus but q_c135ee (V48, α1.4, Δ0.03) TF 64x2/64x1/32x3 beat GRU 64x2; 0.05-0.1 one lab set d128 TF beat GRU 12/12 (−0.28 nats); Δ>=0.1 GRU 7/8. Treat as ~85%, weaker for V>=48 or d_model 128.

regime.note: same optimizer/lr/T; post-LN nn.TransformerEncoderLayer, learned positions; GRU 64x2

K1012.phase: Saturation (smaller Δ>=0.1, larger >=3x; lab): larger-Δ wins bigram 25% (4/16), tabular 43% (63/146, K1021), spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58% (Adam/AdamW same-opt 23/30), univariate 60%. Tabular: below Δ_small 0.03 the larger Δ wins ~95%, at 0.03-0.1 ~75%.

K1017.phase: 0.02≤Δ<0.1: larger d_model wins corpus 11/11, lab 11/12 (robust); at FIXED d_model shallower wins corpus 7/7 (3 q) but deeper wins lab+controlled 9/9 on one V48 set at Δ 0.02-0.05 (q_c135ee: 64x2>64x1) - treat depth as a weak tie-break there. Δ<0.02: more params 12/16 corpus, larger d_ff 2/2, deeper at fixed d_model 5/7.

regime.note: post-LN TransformerEncoderLayer, learned positions, V 24-48; same optimizer/lr/T

K1018.mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.
K1018.phase: dim≥8, Δ≥0.05: shallow beats deep 2/3 (gap≥3, ratio .64), 3/7 (gap<3); smooth act 6/6; more-LN 5/11. dim<8, Δ≥0.05: deeper 7/7. Δ<0.05 any dim: more-LN 7/9, depth rule.

regime.note: small n (≈4 questions); train rows 1024

K1020.mechanism: Each LN rescales block activations to unit RMS, raising the effective step size of the features that bend the boundary; a skip connection preserves the input path but does not speed feature learning. Predicts LN count dominates whenever learning curved features is the bottleneck (most Δ), and residual matters only when plain deep stacks overshoot (high Δ, harder spirals).
K1020.phase: Plain(more LN) vs res(fewer LN): Δ<0.03 res 14/24; 0.03-0.5 plain 25/29; ≥0.5 res 6/10 (lab 5/6, controlled 1/4). Res(0 LN) vs plain(≥1 LN): Δ<0.1 plain 49/56; ≥0.5 res 10/13.

regime.note: Δ = core-rule units; 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 bands have only 3-5 lab sets

K1021.mechanism: Labels are deterministic functions of 2-4 of 16 Gaussian coordinates with only 1024 train rows; by Δ≈0.1 the boundary is fit and further parameter movement mainly inflates logit scale (overconfident test errors) and fits distractor directions. Predicts the reversal is strongest where many noisy directions/interactions exist (sparse_interaction), weakest where a sharp boundary still benefits from more fitting (piecewise), and grows with epochs over the 1024 rows (K1032).
K1021.phase: larger-Δ (≥3×) win rate by smaller Δ (4-epoch lab): <0.03 ~95% (ratio 0.33-0.58); 0.03-0.1 piecewise 88%, smooth 73%, sparse 63% (ratio ~0.8); >=0.1 piecewise 62% (0.93), smooth 40% (1.07), sparse 15% (1.44). At 32 epochs 16-D smooth: Δ≥0.5 loses even to Δ<0.03 (K1032).

regime.note: lab pairs differ in architecture; 104 sets, mostly T=256 bs16 (4 epochs); corpus 5/9 agrees; Δ: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2lr√T, SGD lr·T·0.01/(1-m)

K1022.mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.
K1022.phase: late-LN wins: tabular Δ<0.1 corpus 6/7, lab 3/5; multivariate Δ<0.1 corpus 5/5, lab 1/2; any family Δ>=0.1 3/6; univariate 1/4 corpus + 1/4 controlled; XOR 1/4 corpus, 2/4 lab.

regime.note: equal LN count, equal residual, same optimizer/lr/T; small n, effect ~5-20%

K1032.mechanism: 1024 rows in 16-D (12+ noise coordinates): ~32 passes of Adam lr≥1e-3 drive train CE→0 by fitting noise directions, inflating logit scale so test errors are overconfident (controlled: high-lr test CE worsened 4→32 epochs while low-lr CE improved). smooth_additive has a near-linear component (sin x≈x), so low-Δ nets already reach good CE; interaction/piecewise rules need large movement, offsetting overfit. Predicts: fewer features or ≤8 epochs → large Δ wins again.
K1032.phase: large-Δ(≥0.5) vs low-Δ(0.01-0.15): smooth 16-D 32ep → low wins 3/3 dataflip + 5/6 controlled; smooth 16-D 4ep → low wins 1/172 lab, 0/3 controlled; smooth 2-D 16ep → low 0/3 corpus; sparse 16-D 32ep → low 0/4 dataflip, 4/6 controlled (ratio .88-.94); piecewise 16-D 32ep → low 2/8 corpus.

regime.note: 8-D or 2-D at 32 epochs untested (corpus 2-D smooth at 16 epochs: large Δ wins 3/3)

K1033.mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.
K1033.phase: shallow(2-block) vs deep(4-block), Δ 0.03-0.1: 32 epochs → shallow 16/16 (ratio .59-.75); 4 epochs → 4/8 (.99). Corpus ≥16 epochs: Δ≥0.1 shallow 12/15 (.65); Δ<0.03 shallow 6/17 (1.04).

regime.note: one instance per family; depth confounded with width/LN; piecewise untested

K1038.mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.
K1038.phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

K1039.mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).
K1039.phase: Rectifier (fewer LN) vs SiLU/GELU (more LN), shared SGD regression: LN gap 0 → 17/18; gap 1 → 14/17; gap ≥2 → 12/25 (corpus 1/6; controlled offset target 6/6, trig 4/12). Adam-family: SiLU-more-LN wins 11/16 (corpus).

K1040.mechanism: torch Adam adds wd·w to the gradient before dividing by √v. Once the spiral is fit, data gradients→~0, so the decay term dominates both numerator and v and Adam takes ~lr-sized normalized steps toward zero, capping weight norm and logit margin (CE floor ~1e-3). AdamW shrinks by lr·wd·w (~1e-6/step), negligible. Predicts harm grows with wd, lr and T, and vanishes when data gradients stay large (noisy-label bigram LM, under-trained 3-turn spirals).
K1040.phase: AdamW(wd) vs Adam(coupled wd), same lr/net, spiral: wd1e-3 ratio ~0.03, wd1e-2 ~0.002 (12/12). β2 .999 vs .95 (same wd): lr 3e-3 ratio 5.8, 1e-3 24 (0.95 wins); lr 3e-4 ratio 0.36 (0.999 wins); with LN signs mixed.

regime.note: one controlled architecture + q_6a81f1, q_682517; RMSprop/Adagrad coupled wd untested; 2-3 turn spirals untested

snaps.label: kb_0002
snaps.render:
[K1001] CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
[K1002] Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.
[K1003] SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.
[K1004] LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins only 22/36 corpus pairs (1e-3 univariate 1/4), BUT 6/6 when the RMSprop net has the better MLP (more LN + residual; median MSE ratio 0.04, e.g. q_65db92), 12/22 at equal architecture, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35: prefer it at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe.
[K1005] Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.
[K1006] MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.
[K1007] Regression depth × residual (uni/multivariate MSE, any budget): a deeper residual MLP beats a shallower non-residual one 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 when lr·T<0.1); at equal depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets (sin(2πx)…, cos(2π sin…)) amplify the depth advantage: composition of 4-5 normalized residual blocks generates high-frequency curvature that 1-2 layer nets cannot reach within the budget. Non-residual deep stacks without LN are the exception: they attenuate signal and usually lose.
[K1008] Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Epoch-7 misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets (both also confounded with LN placement). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1009) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.
[K1009] Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.
[K1010] XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so (i) Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied; (ii) among equal optimizers, deep RESIDUAL blocks with LN win: deeper+residual beats shallower plain 33-14 on classification, more-LN wins 20-5 on spiral (Δ≥0.01), deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11). A 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes the plateau in 256-512 steps. Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly everything stuck → pick largest Δ).
[K1011] Bigram LM architecture (same optimizer): a GRU LM beats a post-LN causal transformer in 20 of 21 same-optimizer pairs, at both weak and strong Δ — rank the GRU first. Mechanism: the task is a first-order lookup P(y|x_t); the GRU maps the current token straight to its output state and its tanh-bounded hidden state gives near-uniform initial logits (CE≈ln V), while the post-LN transformer feeds unit-RMS features to the head (logit std ~0.6, initial CE ~ln V+0.1-0.2) and must learn to ignore attention mixing. Transformer-vs-transformer shape is Δ-dependent (see bigram transformer shape rule): fewer layers only reliably wins at 0.02≤Δ<0.1 (21/21); at Δ≥0.5 prefer smaller d_model.
[K1012] When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.
[K1013] Bigram LM optimizer sweet spot: labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gradients carry irreducible noise and the achievable gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V. Among choices with Δ≥0.1, prefer the one with Δ nearest ~0.3 (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, Adagrad 3e-3); treat Δ≥1 (lr≥1e-3 at T≥1024, lr 3e-3 at T≥512) as likely overshoot. Below Δ≈0.1 ordinary max-Δ still applies. This 'nearest 0.3' scoring picks 52/66 bigram optimizer/mixed winners vs 47/66 for plain max-Δ; adaptive-transformer winners are mostly lr 3e-4 (22/52). If all Δ<0.02 every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.
[K1014] Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue): the deeper-is-better preference (under Δ<0.1) is strong for smooth/compositional targets — tabular smooth_additive (deeper 24-8), XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4), oscillatory univariate targets — but weak or absent when the rule is piecewise_boundary (5-6) or sparse_interaction (6-3) or XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7); there prefer the most-LN candidate regardless of depth, EXCEPT XOR with ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05, where more-LN wins only 5/11 and GELU/SiLU decides (6/6; see XOR-distractor rule). Polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.
[K1015] Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: fewest layers wins 21/21 pairs and the larger d_model wins 15/15 (d_model 128 × 1-2 layers, d_ff 256 won 10/10 questions). 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6 and fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (cf. K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17 (deeper-32 beat 64×1 in q_b66719). Winner-level 20/31 vs 18/31 for pooled 'fewer layers'. GRU still beats all (K1011).
[K1018] XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.05, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOW-WIDE beats deep when the depth gap is ≥3 blocks (2-block vs 5-block: corpus 2/3, median CE ratio 0.64; q_bfba99 AdamW 3e-4×512: all three 2-block w192-256 nets beat both 5-block residual nets (3-4 LN), 2-LN SiLU first, 4-LN LeakyReLU last; controlled 4/4). q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17. With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (deeper 7/7); for Δ<0.05 the LN/depth rule holds for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).
[K1019] SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).
[K1020] Two-spiral classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual only as tie-break (K1006 sum). Same residual status: more LN wins at every Δ (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-with-more-LN vs residual-with-fewer-LN: 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 25/29 (lab 16/18, controlled 6/6 ratio 1.03-3.7; q_31abed, q_9c257e C>B; miss q_9c257e D>C); Δ<0.03 near coin flip (residual 14/24: corpus 5/5, lab 9/17, controlled 0/2); Δ≥0.5 mixed (residual lab 5/6, controlled 1/4 — only 2-turn at Δ1.5). Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain nets with ≥1 LN at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59, CE ratio 1.07-1.27), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03, coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).
[K1021] Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples) on 16-D smooth_additive, where Δ 0.01-0.15 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1032). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1009). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1032] Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): on smooth_additive the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices with ≥1 LN: dataflip 3/3 (q_86f129; q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, same net; q_e79cfd plain SGD 1e-3 + 2 LN beat Adam 1e-3); controlled 16-D test CE Adam 1e-3 0.43 vs AdamW 1e-4 0.26-0.30, Adam 3e-5 0.29-0.33. Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction at 32 epochs: larger Δ still usually wins (corpus 6/8, dataflip 4/4) unless Δ≥3.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1040] Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).

K1001.mechanism: Every candidate is under-trained, so loss falls monotonically with how far parameters move from init; adaptive optimizers move ~lr per step regardless of gradient scale, so lr·T measures distance. Predicts the rule saturates once Δ is enough to fit the (tiny, noiseless) train set (~0.1-0.3), after which overconfidence/overshoot dominates - observed in the phase table.
K1001.phase: Largest-Δ (≥3× gap) win rate depends on the smaller Δ: <0.03 ~95% (tabular lab 2011/2135); 0.03-0.1 ~60-88%; once smaller Δ≥0.1 only 25-60% (bigram 25%, tabular 43%, spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58%, univariate 60%; K1012, K1021). LR-ceiling breaks: K1004.

K1004.mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).
K1004.phase: RMSprop≥3e-3 vs ≥3× smaller-Δ choice on MSE: RMSprop net has higher LN+residual score → wins 6/6; equal → 12/22; lower → 4/8. RMSprop 1e-3 univariate 1/4.

regime.note: (a) corpus regression pairs; (b) bigram post-LN transformer vs GRU

K1006.mechanism: Each unnormalized pre-activation layer shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU at init), so an under-trained deep stack feeds a weak signal to the head; pre-LN restores unit scale and identity paths keep gradient flow, speeding an under-trained net 2-3x. Predicts the LN advantage shrinks once Δ is large enough to learn the scale (tabular Δ>=0.1 reverses, K1009) and where LN destroys label-relevant norm information (2-D spiral, K1020).
K1006.phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12, tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); spiral plain+LN vs residual: residual 7/9 (K1020); XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10 (weak).

regime.note: tabular only when Δ<0.1; spiral handled by K1020; same optimizer/lr/T

K1008.mechanism: SiLU/GELU have derivative ≈0.5 at 0 and sub-unit gain over typical pre-activations, so each un-normalized block shrinks signal and gradient (≈0.5^depth), slowing fitting in an under-trained regime; ReLU-family keep gain ~1 on the active side. Predicts the SiLU penalty shrinks when every block has LN (re-scales) and grows with depth of unnormalized stacks; on classification with distractors the smooth curvature regularizes confidence instead, flipping the sign (K1009/K1018).

regime.note: corpus same-optimizer pairs; activation pairs often confounded with depth/LN

K1011.mechanism: The GRU maps the current token straight to a tanh-bounded state (initial CE≈ln V), so it leads whenever little is learned (small Δ). A post-LN transformer starts ~0.1-0.2 nats worse but its wider embedding/FFN path learns the lookup faster once Δ is moderate; at Δ≥0.15 wide post-LN transformers overshoot (cf. K1004b, K1017), restoring the GRU lead. Predicts the window shifts with d_model (wider overshoots earlier).
K1011.phase: Δ<0.05: GRU 10/10 (corpus). 0.05≤Δ<0.15: tf with d_model≥GRU width 20/20; narrower tf loses 12/13. Δ≥0.15: GRU 6/6 corpus + 4/4 lab (d128×2 tf lost by 0.33 at Δ0.307 after winning by 0.15 at Δ0.077, same data).

regime.note: plain SGD (Δ~0.005) mixed 2/4 in lab; V 24-48, ctx 12-16

K1012.phase: Saturation (smaller Δ>=0.1, larger >=3x; lab): larger-Δ wins bigram 25% (4/16), tabular 43% (63/146, K1021), spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58% (Adam/AdamW same-opt 23/30), univariate 60%. Tabular: below Δ_small 0.03 the larger Δ wins ~95%, at 0.03-0.1 ~75%.

K1017.phase: 0.02≤Δ<0.1: larger d_model wins corpus 11/11, lab 11/12 (robust); at FIXED d_model shallower wins corpus 7/7 (3 q) but deeper wins lab+controlled 9/9 on one V48 set at Δ 0.02-0.05 (q_c135ee: 64x2>64x1) - treat depth as a weak tie-break there. Δ<0.02: more params 12/16 corpus, larger d_ff 2/2, deeper at fixed d_model 5/7.

regime.note: post-LN TransformerEncoderLayer, learned positions, V 24-48; same optimizer/lr/T

K1018.mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.
K1018.phase: dim≥8, Δ≥0.05: shallow beats deep 2/3 (gap≥3, ratio .64), 3/7 (gap<3); smooth act 6/6; more-LN 5/11. dim<8, Δ≥0.05: deeper 7/7. Δ<0.05 any dim: more-LN 7/9, depth rule.

regime.note: small n (≈4 questions); train rows 1024

K1021.mechanism: Labels are deterministic functions of 2-4 of 16 Gaussian coordinates with only 1024 train rows; by Δ≈0.1 the boundary is fit and further parameter movement mainly inflates logit scale (overconfident test errors) and fits distractor directions. Predicts the reversal is strongest where many noisy directions/interactions exist (sparse_interaction), weakest where a sharp boundary still benefits from more fitting (piecewise), and grows with epochs over the 1024 rows (K1032).
K1021.phase: larger-Δ (≥3×) win rate by smaller Δ (4-epoch lab): <0.03 ~95% (ratio 0.33-0.58); 0.03-0.1 piecewise 88%, smooth 73%, sparse 63% (ratio ~0.8); >=0.1 piecewise 62% (0.93), smooth 40% (1.07), sparse 15% (1.44). At 32 epochs 16-D smooth: Δ≥0.5 loses even to Δ<0.03 (K1032).

regime.note: lab pairs differ in architecture; 104 sets, mostly T=256 bs16 (4 epochs); corpus 5/9 agrees; Δ: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2lr√T, SGD lr·T·0.01/(1-m)

K1022.mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.
K1022.phase: late-LN wins: tabular Δ<0.1 corpus 6/7, lab 3/5; multivariate Δ<0.1 corpus 5/5, lab 1/2; any family Δ>=0.1 3/6; univariate 1/4 corpus + 1/4 controlled; XOR 1/4 corpus, 2/4 lab.

regime.note: equal LN count, equal residual, same optimizer/lr/T; small n, effect ~5-20%

K1038.mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.
K1038.phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

K1039.mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).
K1039.phase: Rectifier (fewer LN) vs SiLU/GELU (more LN), shared SGD regression: LN gap 0 → 17/18; gap 1 → 14/17; gap ≥2 → 12/25 (corpus 1/6; controlled offset target 6/6, trig 4/12). Adam-family: SiLU-more-LN wins 11/16 (corpus).

K1041.mechanism: Zero linear signal: CE sits on the ln2 plateau until weights travel far enough from init to bend the boundary, so escape time is set by displacement Δ, which dominates any per-step architectural efficiency (≤1.3× CE effect). Once optimizers are equal, LN keeps per-block pre-activations O(1) so all blocks contribute curvature; residual paths only matter when Δ is too small for plain stacks to start moving (Δ<0.03) or LN is absent.
K1041.phase: Mixed optimizers: ≥3× Δ wins 78/79 (spiral). Equal optimizer: plain+more-LN vs residual+fewer-LN — Δ<0.03 residual 14/24; 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain 25/29; Δ≥0.5 mixed. 0-LN residual vs ≥1-LN plain: loses 51/59 at Δ<0.5, wins 10/13 at Δ≥0.5. 1 turn & Δ≥0.5: CE ≤1e-4, decided by confidence tail (coupled wd, β2), not Δ.

regime.note: Δ in core-rule units (K1001/K1019); turns 1-3; SGD with 0 LN gets far less credit (K1038); XOR ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05: K1018

K1042.mechanism: Adagrad's accumulator grows ~t·g², so step ~lr/√t and Δ≈2·lr·√T; SGD steps scale with raw gradient size (|g|≈0.003 LM embeddings, 0.01 classification, 0.03 MSE with momentum) instead of being normalised to ~lr, so its credit depends on loss scale and on LN keeping gradients O(1).

regime.note: all families; SGD calibrations fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs

K1043.mechanism: Before the boundary is learned (Δ<0.1), test CE tracks optimisation progress, which LN and composed depth speed up; after it is learned, the residual CE is dominated by overconfident errors on 1024 rows, which deep/LN'd nets amplify by growing logits faster, so capacity-limited shallow smooth nets win.
K1043.phase: Δ<0.1: more-LN 41-4, deeper 35-17 (smooth_additive 24-8, piecewise 5-6, sparse 6-3). Δ≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, GELU/SiLU 16/16.

regime.note: mostly 4 epochs (4096-8192 samples); at 32 epochs the reversal starts at Δ≈0.03 (K1032)

K1044.mechanism: MSE fitting of curved targets needs composed nonlinearities, and with LN a plain stack still propagates signal, so depth pays even without skips; under CE the plain deep stack's attenuated/ill-conditioned gradients slow the margin growth that test CE rewards, while residual paths keep an identity route.
K1044.phase: Regression: deeper wins regardless of residual (32-2 residual, 24-15 plain) unless 0 LN. Classification: residual decides (shallow-res > deep-plain 19-13). Tabular shared Δ≥0.1 or 32 epochs: shallow wins (K1043, long-budget rule).

K1045.mechanism: With 32 passes over 1024 rows, large-Δ nets memorise and inflate logits, so test CE is dominated by confident errors; the bias-variance optimum moves to modest Δ, and depth/LN that speed logit growth hurt earlier than at 4 epochs.
K1045.phase: 32 epochs: Δ<0.03 loses to 0.03-0.15 (6/6); 0.03-0.15 beats ≥0.5 (14/14 lab); depth: shallow wins from Δ≈0.03 (16/16). 4 epochs (T=256 bs16): Δ<0.03 loses 171/172; depth coin flip at Δ0.03-0.1.

regime.note: piecewise_boundary at 32 epochs: larger Δ usually still wins (corpus 6/8) unless Δ≥3

K1046.mechanism: When CE→1e-4 the data gradient collapses, so the coupled L2 term wd·θ dominates Adam's numerator AND its second-moment denominator, turning the step into normalised weight shrinkage that caps logit growth; AdamW decouples decay so it is ≈wd=0. Predicts the penalty appears only when data gradients are tiny (separable, low-turn, long T) and is absent on noisy-label tasks (bigram LM) or unsaturated spirals.
K1046.phase: Coupled-wd penalty (1-turn spiral, T=2048): wd1e-5 2-2.6×, 1e-4 15-21×, 1e-3 59-182×. Low-lr AdamW 3e-5 β2.95 vs Adam wd0 lr1e-3: wins at T=2048 (2/2), loses at T=1024 (2/2). Outside CE-saturating tasks: wd/β2/Adam-vs-AdamW effects <1%.

regime.note: exception measured only on 1-turn spiral (lab: plain ReLU d2 w48 lr3e-3; controlled: 3-block LN GELU / 4-block SiLU, lr1e-3, T 1024-2048)

snaps.label: kb_0002（候选，被拒）
snaps.render:
[K1001] CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1042), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
[K1004] LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins only 22/36 corpus pairs (1e-3 univariate 1/4), BUT 6/6 when the RMSprop net has the better MLP (more LN + residual; median MSE ratio 0.04, e.g. q_65db92), 12/22 at equal architecture, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35: prefer it at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe.
[K1006] MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1041); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1043/K1021.
[K1008] Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Epoch-7 misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets (both also confounded with LN placement). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1043) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.
[K1011] Bigram LM, GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): the GRU wins OUTSIDE the window 0.05≤Δ<0.15 (core-rule units) — corpus 16/16 pairs at Δ<0.05 or ≥0.15, incl. vs 1-2-layer d_model-64 transformers (q_932238, q_6d6c08, q_037941); lab adaptive 4/4. INSIDE the window a transformer whose d_model ≥ the GRU's hidden width beats it 20/20 pairs over 5 datasets (q_1e3031 Adagrad 1e-3×1024: tf 64×1 > GRU64 1-layer > GRU64 2-layer; lab d128×3 beat GRU by 0.12-0.49 nats), while narrower transformers (d32 vs GRU64) still lose 12/13. At equal width a 1-layer GRU beats a 2-layer GRU (lab 3/3, q_1e3031).
[K1012] When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.
[K1013] Bigram LM optimizer sweet spot: labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gradients carry irreducible noise and the achievable gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V. Among choices with Δ≥0.1, prefer the one with Δ nearest ~0.3 (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, Adagrad 3e-3); treat Δ≥1 (lr≥1e-3 at T≥1024, lr 3e-3 at T≥512) as likely overshoot. Below Δ≈0.1 ordinary max-Δ still applies. This 'nearest 0.3' scoring picks 52/66 bigram optimizer/mixed winners vs 47/66 for plain max-Δ; adaptive-transformer winners are mostly lr 3e-4 (22/52). If all Δ<0.02 every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: fewest layers wins 21/21 pairs and larger d_model 15/15 (d_model 128 × 1-2 layers, d_ff 256 won 10/10 questions). 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6, fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17. Heads (else equal): 2 heads beat 4 (lab 5/6; q_140f05, q_e83d98, q_84f859 3/3; gap ≤0.07, often <0.001). GRU: K1011.
[K1018] XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.05, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOW-WIDE beats deep when the depth gap is ≥3 blocks (2-block vs 5-block: corpus 2/3, median CE ratio 0.64; q_bfba99 AdamW 3e-4×512: all three 2-block w192-256 nets beat both 5-block residual nets (3-4 LN), 2-LN SiLU first, 4-LN LeakyReLU last; controlled 4/4). q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17. With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (deeper 7/7); for Δ<0.05 the LN/depth rule holds for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).
[K1021] Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples), where Δ 0.03-0.3 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1045). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1043). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1038] SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1042 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1041] Two-spiral / XOR classification (chance CE=ln2): when optimizer, lr or T differ, rank by core-rule Δ FIRST: a ≥3× larger Δ wins 78/79 corpus spiral pairs and max-Δ picks 30/33 mixed spiral winners (misses: 0-LN plain SGD, K1038; ties). Δ≲0.01 nets sit at CE 0.65-0.70 (tied bottom block). ONLY at equal optimizer/lr/T use architecture: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.8-0.9); plain+more-LN beats residual+fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5 (25/29), residual leads at Δ<0.03 (14/24); 0-LN residual wins only at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Deeper wins XOR (26-11). Best CE: 1 turn 1e-3-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.5, 3 turns ~0.6. 1-turn at Δ≥0.5 = confidence-tail regime (coupled-wd exception, K1046).
[K1042] Optimizer conversion for the Δ rule (K1001). Adagrad: steps decay ~lr/√t, so it equals Adam only at ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger lr — same arch, lr ratio ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70, 10× coin flip, ≥30× Adagrad 9/9; within Adagrad larger lr wins 40/41 (3e-3 never too big); Adagrad lr≤1e-4 is frozen. SGD: plain (m=0) lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins 3/141 pairs vs a >15× larger adaptive Δ; LM CE stays ≈ln V). SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10 on classification (131/146), lr/3 on MSE regression (59/71; beats Adagrad ≤1e-3 and Adam ≤1e-4), lr/30 on bigram LM (68/70; beats Adam-family 1/18). These credits assume ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less (K1038).
[K1043] Tabular classification depth/LN rule (1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ in core-rule units, NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad). Shared Δ<0.1: normal rule — more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17, strongest on smooth_additive (deeper 24-8; q_1a7ca0 2-block 2-LN beat 1-block wide 1-LN), absent on piecewise_boundary (5-6) and sparse_interaction (6-3): there pick most-LN regardless of depth. Shared Δ≥0.1: boundary already learned, CE set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider GELU/SiLU nets with fewer LN: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. Picks 26/32 arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse (XOR ≤4 features: deeper 15-4).
[K1044] Depth × residual × task (MLPs, same optimizer). MSE regression: depth helps even without residuals — deeper residual beats shallower plain 32-2, deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15, deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 at lr·T<0.1); equal-depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets amplify the depth edge; deep plain stacks with 0 LN are the exception (signal attenuation). Classification (CE): depth WITHOUT residual hurts — shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13, deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14 (exceptions: spiral plain with more LN, K1041; tabular Δ≥0.1 reverses depth, K1043).
[K1045] Tabular LONG budget (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): optimum Δ≈0.03-0.3; Δ≥0.5 (Adam-family lr≥1e-3 at T≥512) loses — lab smooth_additive Δ0.03-0.15 beats Δ0.5-1.5 8/8 (CE ratio 1.47), sparse 6/6; dataflip 4/4 (q_86f129, q_565490, q_e79cfd, q_f05f74 RMSprop 1e-4 + LN beat Adam 1e-3); q_b070ff AdamW 1e-3×2048 (Δ2) last, Adagrad 3e-3 3-LN residual (Δ0.27) first. Δ<0.03 still loses to Δ0.03-0.15 (6/6). Depth reverses early: shallow 2-block wide beats 4-block already at Δ0.03-0.1 (16/16, ratio 0.59-0.75; q_eeb76a); among shallow more LN wins, among deep residual > plain. At 4 epochs see K1021.
[K1046] Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (higher wd 3-10, all within 1%), Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas 5-5, β2 0.95 vs 0.999 ~even (7-4). Never let them override a Δ gap; order near-twins by architecture. EXCEPTION — CE→1e-4 regime (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family Δ≥0.5): torch Adam with COUPLED weight_decay≥1e-4 loses to its AdamW or wd=0 twin (lab+controlled 36/36; CE ratio ~10× at wd 1e-4, 56× at 1e-3, 800× at 1e-2; q_6a81f1) and at T=2048 even to AdamW 3e-5 β2 0.95 (Δ0.06; q_65d623; controlled 2/2, but not at T=1024). AdamW at the same lr ≈ wd=0. Not seen on bigram LM.

K1001.mechanism: Every candidate is under-trained, so loss falls monotonically with how far parameters move from init; adaptive optimizers move ~lr per step regardless of gradient scale, so lr·T measures distance. Predicts the rule saturates once Δ is enough to fit the (tiny, noiseless) train set (~0.1-0.3), after which overconfidence/overshoot dominates - observed in the phase table.
K1001.phase: Largest-Δ (≥3× gap) win rate depends on the smaller Δ: <0.03 ~95% (tabular lab 2011/2135); 0.03-0.1 ~60-88%; once smaller Δ≥0.1 only 25-60% (bigram 25%, tabular 43%, spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58%, univariate 60%; K1012, K1021). LR-ceiling breaks: K1004.

K1004.mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).
K1004.phase: RMSprop≥3e-3 vs ≥3× smaller-Δ choice on MSE: RMSprop net has higher LN+residual score → wins 6/6; equal → 12/22; lower → 4/8. RMSprop 1e-3 univariate 1/4.

regime.note: (a) corpus regression pairs; (b) bigram post-LN transformer vs GRU

K1006.mechanism: Each unnormalized pre-activation layer shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU at init), so an under-trained deep stack feeds a weak signal to the head; pre-LN restores unit scale and identity paths keep gradient flow, speeding an under-trained net 2-3x. Predicts the LN advantage shrinks once Δ is large enough to learn the scale (tabular Δ>=0.1 reverses, K1009) and where LN destroys label-relevant norm information (2-D spiral, K1020).
K1006.phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12, tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); spiral plain+LN vs residual: residual 7/9 (K1020); XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10 (weak).

regime.note: tabular only when Δ<0.1; spiral handled by K1020; same optimizer/lr/T

K1008.mechanism: SiLU/GELU have derivative ≈0.5 at 0 and sub-unit gain over typical pre-activations, so each un-normalized block shrinks signal and gradient (≈0.5^depth), slowing fitting in an under-trained regime; ReLU-family keep gain ~1 on the active side. Predicts the SiLU penalty shrinks when every block has LN (re-scales) and grows with depth of unnormalized stacks; on classification with distractors the smooth curvature regularizes confidence instead, flipping the sign (K1009/K1018).

regime.note: corpus same-optimizer pairs; activation pairs often confounded with depth/LN

K1009.mechanism: With 1024 rows and labels set by 2-4 coordinates, once Δ≥0.1 the decision boundary is already fit; test CE is then set by logit scale on misclassified points, so anything that speeds fitting (depth, LN, ReLU kinks, larger lr) inflates confidence. Predicts the same reversal for optimizer Δ (K1021) and no reversal on XOR/spiral where the boundary is still being learned.
K1009.phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ per core rule

K1011.phase: GRU-vs-post-LN-TF same optimizer: corpus GRU 20/21; Δ<0.01 GRU 8/10 (lab+corpus); 0.02-0.05 GRU 2/2 corpus but q_c135ee (V48, α1.4, Δ0.03) TF 64x2/64x1/32x3 beat GRU 64x2; 0.05-0.1 one lab set d128 TF beat GRU 12/12 (−0.28 nats); Δ>=0.1 GRU 7/8. Treat as ~85%, weaker for V>=48 or d_model 128.

regime.note: same optimizer/lr/T; post-LN nn.TransformerEncoderLayer, learned positions; GRU 64x2

K1012.phase: Saturation (smaller Δ>=0.1, larger >=3x; lab): larger-Δ wins bigram 25% (4/16), tabular 43% (63/146, K1021), spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58% (Adam/AdamW same-opt 23/30), univariate 60%. Tabular: below Δ_small 0.03 the larger Δ wins ~95%, at 0.03-0.1 ~75%.

K1017.phase: 0.02≤Δ<0.1: larger d_model wins corpus 11/11, lab 11/12 (robust); at FIXED d_model shallower wins corpus 7/7 (3 q) but deeper wins lab+controlled 9/9 on one V48 set at Δ 0.02-0.05 (q_c135ee: 64x2>64x1) - treat depth as a weak tie-break there. Δ<0.02: more params 12/16 corpus, larger d_ff 2/2, deeper at fixed d_model 5/7.

regime.note: post-LN TransformerEncoderLayer, learned positions, V 24-48; same optimizer/lr/T

K1018.mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.
K1018.phase: dim≥8, Δ≥0.05: shallow beats deep 2/3 (gap≥3, ratio .64), 3/7 (gap<3); smooth act 6/6; more-LN 5/11. dim<8, Δ≥0.05: deeper 7/7. Δ<0.05 any dim: more-LN 7/9, depth rule.

regime.note: small n (≈4 questions); train rows 1024

K1020.mechanism: Each LN rescales block activations to unit RMS, raising the effective step size of the features that bend the boundary; a skip connection preserves the input path but does not speed feature learning. Predicts LN count dominates whenever learning curved features is the bottleneck (most Δ), and residual matters only when plain deep stacks overshoot (high Δ, harder spirals).
K1020.phase: Plain(more LN) vs res(fewer LN): Δ<0.03 res 14/24; 0.03-0.5 plain 25/29; ≥0.5 res 6/10 (lab 5/6, controlled 1/4). Res(0 LN) vs plain(≥1 LN): Δ<0.1 plain 49/56; ≥0.5 res 10/13.

regime.note: Δ = core-rule units; 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 bands have only 3-5 lab sets

K1021.mechanism: Labels are deterministic functions of 2-4 of 16 Gaussian coordinates with only 1024 train rows; by Δ≈0.1 the boundary is fit and further parameter movement mainly inflates logit scale (overconfident test errors) and fits distractor directions. Predicts the reversal is strongest where many noisy directions/interactions exist (sparse_interaction), weakest where a sharp boundary still benefits from more fitting (piecewise), and grows with epochs over the 1024 rows (K1032).
K1021.phase: larger-Δ (≥3×) win rate by smaller Δ (4-epoch lab): <0.03 ~95% (ratio 0.33-0.58); 0.03-0.1 piecewise 88%, smooth 73%, sparse 63% (ratio ~0.8); >=0.1 piecewise 62% (0.93), smooth 40% (1.07), sparse 15% (1.44). At 32 epochs 16-D smooth: Δ≥0.5 loses even to Δ<0.03 (K1032).

regime.note: lab pairs differ in architecture; 104 sets, mostly T=256 bs16 (4 epochs); corpus 5/9 agrees; Δ: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2lr√T, SGD lr·T·0.01/(1-m)

K1022.mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.
K1022.phase: late-LN wins: tabular Δ<0.1 corpus 6/7, lab 3/5; multivariate Δ<0.1 corpus 5/5, lab 1/2; any family Δ>=0.1 3/6; univariate 1/4 corpus + 1/4 controlled; XOR 1/4 corpus, 2/4 lab.

regime.note: equal LN count, equal residual, same optimizer/lr/T; small n, effect ~5-20%

K1032.mechanism: 1024 rows in 16-D (12+ noise coordinates): ~32 passes of Adam lr≥1e-3 drive train CE→0 by fitting noise directions, inflating logit scale so test errors are overconfident (controlled: high-lr test CE worsened 4→32 epochs while low-lr CE improved). smooth_additive has a near-linear component (sin x≈x), so low-Δ nets already reach good CE; interaction/piecewise rules need large movement, offsetting overfit. Predicts: fewer features or ≤8 epochs → large Δ wins again.
K1032.phase: large-Δ(≥0.5) vs low-Δ(0.01-0.15): smooth 16-D 32ep → low wins 3/3 dataflip + 5/6 controlled; smooth 16-D 4ep → low wins 1/172 lab, 0/3 controlled; smooth 2-D 16ep → low 0/3 corpus; sparse 16-D 32ep → low 0/4 dataflip, 4/6 controlled (ratio .88-.94); piecewise 16-D 32ep → low 2/8 corpus.

regime.note: 8-D or 2-D at 32 epochs untested (corpus 2-D smooth at 16 epochs: large Δ wins 3/3)

K1033.mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.
K1033.phase: shallow(2-block) vs deep(4-block), Δ 0.03-0.1: 32 epochs → shallow 16/16 (ratio .59-.75); 4 epochs → 4/8 (.99). Corpus ≥16 epochs: Δ≥0.1 shallow 12/15 (.65); Δ<0.03 shallow 6/17 (1.04).

regime.note: one instance per family; depth confounded with width/LN; piecewise untested

K1038.mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.
K1038.phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

K1039.mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).
K1039.phase: Rectifier (fewer LN) vs SiLU/GELU (more LN), shared SGD regression: LN gap 0 → 17/18; gap 1 → 14/17; gap ≥2 → 12/25 (corpus 1/6; controlled offset target 6/6, trig 4/12). Adam-family: SiLU-more-LN wins 11/16 (corpus).

K1040.mechanism: torch Adam adds wd·w to the gradient before dividing by √v. Once the spiral is fit, data gradients→~0, so the decay term dominates both numerator and v and Adam takes ~lr-sized normalized steps toward zero, capping weight norm and logit margin (CE floor ~1e-3). AdamW shrinks by lr·wd·w (~1e-6/step), negligible. Predicts harm grows with wd, lr and T, and vanishes when data gradients stay large (noisy-label bigram LM, under-trained 3-turn spirals).
K1040.phase: AdamW(wd) vs Adam(coupled wd), same lr/net, spiral: wd1e-3 ratio ~0.03, wd1e-2 ~0.002 (12/12). β2 .999 vs .95 (same wd): lr 3e-3 ratio 5.8, 1e-3 24 (0.95 wins); lr 3e-4 ratio 0.36 (0.999 wins); with LN signs mixed.

regime.note: one controlled architecture + q_6a81f1, q_682517; RMSprop/Adagrad coupled wd untested; 2-3 turn spirals untested

snaps.render:
[K1001] CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
[K1002] Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.
[K1003] SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.
[K1004] LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins only 22/36 corpus pairs (1e-3 univariate 1/4), BUT 6/6 when the RMSprop net has the better MLP (more LN + residual; median MSE ratio 0.04, e.g. q_65db92), 12/22 at equal architecture, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35: prefer it at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe.
[K1005] Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.
[K1006] MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.
[K1007] Regression depth × residual (uni/multivariate MSE, any budget): a deeper residual MLP beats a shallower non-residual one 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 when lr·T<0.1); at equal depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets (sin(2πx)…, cos(2π sin…)) amplify the depth advantage: composition of 4-5 normalized residual blocks generates high-frequency curvature that 1-2 layer nets cannot reach within the budget. Non-residual deep stacks without LN are the exception: they attenuate signal and usually lose.
[K1008] Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Epoch-7 misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets (both also confounded with LN placement). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1009) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.
[K1009] Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.
[K1010] XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so (i) Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied; (ii) among equal optimizers, deep RESIDUAL blocks with LN win: deeper+residual beats shallower plain 33-14 on classification, more-LN wins 20-5 on spiral (Δ≥0.01), deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11). A 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes the plateau in 256-512 steps. Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly everything stuck → pick largest Δ).
[K1011] Bigram LM architecture (same optimizer): a GRU LM beats a post-LN causal transformer in 20 of 21 same-optimizer pairs, at both weak and strong Δ — rank the GRU first. Mechanism: the task is a first-order lookup P(y|x_t); the GRU maps the current token straight to its output state and its tanh-bounded hidden state gives near-uniform initial logits (CE≈ln V), while the post-LN transformer feeds unit-RMS features to the head (logit std ~0.6, initial CE ~ln V+0.1-0.2) and must learn to ignore attention mixing. Transformer-vs-transformer shape is Δ-dependent (see bigram transformer shape rule): fewer layers only reliably wins at 0.02≤Δ<0.1 (21/21); at Δ≥0.5 prefer smaller d_model.
[K1012] When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.
[K1013] Bigram LM optimizer sweet spot: labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gradients carry irreducible noise and the achievable gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V. Among choices with Δ≥0.1, prefer the one with Δ nearest ~0.3 (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, Adagrad 3e-3); treat Δ≥1 (lr≥1e-3 at T≥1024, lr 3e-3 at T≥512) as likely overshoot. Below Δ≈0.1 ordinary max-Δ still applies. This 'nearest 0.3' scoring picks 52/66 bigram optimizer/mixed winners vs 47/66 for plain max-Δ; adaptive-transformer winners are mostly lr 3e-4 (22/52). If all Δ<0.02 every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.
[K1014] Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue): the deeper-is-better preference (under Δ<0.1) is strong for smooth/compositional targets — tabular smooth_additive (deeper 24-8), XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4), oscillatory univariate targets — but weak or absent when the rule is piecewise_boundary (5-6) or sparse_interaction (6-3) or XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7); there prefer the most-LN candidate regardless of depth, EXCEPT XOR with ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05, where more-LN wins only 5/11 and GELU/SiLU decides (6/6; see XOR-distractor rule). Polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.
[K1015] Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: fewest layers wins 21/21 pairs and the larger d_model wins 15/15 (d_model 128 × 1-2 layers, d_ff 256 won 10/10 questions). 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6 and fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (cf. K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17 (deeper-32 beat 64×1 in q_b66719). Winner-level 20/31 vs 18/31 for pooled 'fewer layers'. GRU still beats all (K1011).
[K1018] XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.05, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOW-WIDE beats deep when the depth gap is ≥3 blocks (2-block vs 5-block: corpus 2/3, median CE ratio 0.64; q_bfba99 AdamW 3e-4×512: all three 2-block w192-256 nets beat both 5-block residual nets (3-4 LN), 2-LN SiLU first, 4-LN LeakyReLU last; controlled 4/4). q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17. With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (deeper 7/7); for Δ<0.05 the LN/depth rule holds for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).
[K1019] SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).
[K1020] Two-spiral classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual only as tie-break (K1006 sum). Same residual status: more LN wins at every Δ (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-with-more-LN vs residual-with-fewer-LN: 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 25/29 (lab 16/18, controlled 6/6 ratio 1.03-3.7; q_31abed, q_9c257e C>B; miss q_9c257e D>C); Δ<0.03 near coin flip (residual 14/24: corpus 5/5, lab 9/17, controlled 0/2); Δ≥0.5 mixed (residual lab 5/6, controlled 1/4 — only 2-turn at Δ1.5). Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain nets with ≥1 LN at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59, CE ratio 1.07-1.27), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03, coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).
[K1021] Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples) on 16-D smooth_additive, where Δ 0.01-0.15 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1032). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1009). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1032] Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): on smooth_additive the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices with ≥1 LN: dataflip 3/3 (q_86f129; q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, same net; q_e79cfd plain SGD 1e-3 + 2 LN beat Adam 1e-3); controlled 16-D test CE Adam 1e-3 0.43 vs AdamW 1e-4 0.26-0.30, Adam 3e-5 0.29-0.33. Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction at 32 epochs: larger Δ still usually wins (corpus 6/8, dataflip 4/4) unless Δ≥3.
