texts: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins only 22/36 corpus pairs (1e-3 univariate 1/4), BUT 6/6 when the RMSprop net has the better MLP (more LN + residual; median MSE ratio 0.04, e.g. q_65db92), 12/22 at equal architecture, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35: prefer it at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe.

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

Regression depth × residual (uni/multivariate MSE, any budget): a deeper residual MLP beats a shallower non-residual one 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 when lr·T<0.1); at equal depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: fewest layers wins 21/21 pairs and the larger d_model wins 15/15 (d_model 128 × 1-2 layers, d_ff 256 won 10/10 questions). 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6 and fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (cf. K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17 (deeper-32 beat 64×1 in q_b66719). Winner-level 20/31 vs 18/31 for pooled 'fewer layers'. GRU still beats all (K1011).

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.05, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOW-WIDE beats deep when the depth gap is ≥3 blocks (2-block vs 5-block: corpus 2/3, median CE ratio 0.64; q_bfba99 AdamW 3e-4×512: all three 2-block w192-256 nets beat both 5-block residual nets (3-4 LN), 2-LN SiLU first, 4-LN LeakyReLU last; controlled 4/4). q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17. With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (deeper 7/7); for Δ<0.05 the LN/depth rule holds for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).

SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).

Two-spiral classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual only as tie-break (K1006 sum). Same residual status: more LN wins at every Δ (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-with-more-LN vs residual-with-fewer-LN: 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 25/29 (lab 16/18, controlled 6/6 ratio 1.03-3.7; q_31abed, q_9c257e C>B; miss q_9c257e D>C); Δ<0.03 near coin flip (residual 14/24: corpus 5/5, lab 9/17, controlled 0/2); Δ≥0.5 mixed (residual lab 5/6, controlled 1/4 — only 2-turn at Δ1.5). Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain nets with ≥1 LN at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59, CE ratio 1.07-1.27), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03, coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).

Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples) on 16-D smooth_additive, where Δ 0.01-0.15 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1032). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1009). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).

LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.

Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): on smooth_additive the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices with ≥1 LN: dataflip 3/3 (q_86f129; q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, same net; q_e79cfd plain SGD 1e-3 + 2 LN beat Adam 1e-3); controlled 16-D test CE Adam 1e-3 0.43 vs AdamW 1e-4 0.26-0.30, Adam 3e-5 0.29-0.33. Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction at 32 epochs: larger Δ still usually wins (corpus 6/8, dataflip 4/4) unless Δ≥3.

Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).

SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).

SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).

Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; ratio 0.04, q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35 overall: prefer it over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe. (d) UNIVARIATE regression on a wide (≥128) multi-layer net: Adam-family lr·T≥0.5 overshoots (wide-net univariate ceiling rule).

Bigram LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): the GRU edge depends on d_model. GRU d_model > transformer's (GRU 64 vs T 32): GRU wins 19/20 (corpus 9/9, lab 10/11; q_ce881e GRU64×1 1st). Transformer d_model larger (T128 vs GRU 32/64): transformer wins 13/14 (lab). Equal d_model: toss-up (corpus GRU64×2 vs T64 9/10, lab 1/6; q_ce881e GRU32×2 beat only 1 of 3 d32 transformers) — lean GRU only at d_model 64. Within transformers use the bigram transformer shape rule (K1017).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model → fewer layers wins: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a), Δ≥0.5 8/11, 0.02≤Δ<0.1 8/15 (corpus 5/5, lab 3/10); Δ<0.02 all ≈ln V, deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE — wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger d_model wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512) smaller d_model wins 5/6 — wide post-LN overshoots (K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213). GRU vs transformer: K1011.

Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 8-16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): on smooth_additive the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices: lab 24/28 pairs (7 sets, median CE ratio 0.87); dataflip 4/4 (q_86f129; q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, same net; q_e79cfd plain SGD 1e-3 + 2 LN beat Adam 1e-3; q_07b812 8-D: AdamW 3e-5×1024 beat AdamW 1e-3 and RMSprop 3e-3 on the same w192 net). Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction at 32 epochs: mixed (larger Δ wins corpus 9/11 but lab 3/14) — decide by architecture (K1009/K1033).

UNIVARIATE regression, WIDE multi-layer MLP (width≥128, depth≥2), choices differ in optimizer/lr: lr·T≥1 OVERSHOOTS — prefer a choice with Δ≈0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3) over Adam/AdamW/RMSprop at Δ≥1. Corpus optimizer-only 5/5 (q_3d7396 Adagrad 3e-3 beat AdamW 3e-3; q_9e733e; RMSprop lost 3/3); lab same-arch 8/9 (MSE ratio 3.4); controlled d2-4 w128-256 11/12 (13-1000×); q_2deb46. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and loses (q_f609cc: Adam 3e-3 beat Adam 3e-5, d2 w256; lab 3/7) unless the high side has Δ≥5. NOT for 1-layer or narrow (≤96) nets (larger Δ wins corpus 10/10) nor multivariate regression (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10).

CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1042), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1041); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1043/K1021.

Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Epoch-7 misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets (both also confounded with LN placement). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1043) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.

Bigram LM, GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): the GRU wins OUTSIDE the window 0.05≤Δ<0.15 (core-rule units) — corpus 16/16 pairs at Δ<0.05 or ≥0.15, incl. vs 1-2-layer d_model-64 transformers (q_932238, q_6d6c08, q_037941); lab adaptive 4/4. INSIDE the window a transformer whose d_model ≥ the GRU's hidden width beats it 20/20 pairs over 5 datasets (q_1e3031 Adagrad 1e-3×1024: tf 64×1 > GRU64 1-layer > GRU64 2-layer; lab d128×3 beat GRU by 0.12-0.49 nats), while narrower transformers (d32 vs GRU64) still lose 12/13. At equal width a 1-layer GRU beats a 2-layer GRU (lab 3/3, q_1e3031).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: fewest layers wins 21/21 pairs and larger d_model 15/15 (d_model 128 × 1-2 layers, d_ff 256 won 10/10 questions). 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6, fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17. Heads (else equal): 2 heads beat 4 (lab 5/6; q_140f05, q_e83d98, q_84f859 3/3; gap ≤0.07, often <0.001). GRU: K1011.

Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples), where Δ 0.03-0.3 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1045). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1043). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).

SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1042 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).

Two-spiral / XOR classification (chance CE=ln2): when optimizer, lr or T differ, rank by core-rule Δ FIRST: a ≥3× larger Δ wins 78/79 corpus spiral pairs and max-Δ picks 30/33 mixed spiral winners (misses: 0-LN plain SGD, K1038; ties). Δ≲0.01 nets sit at CE 0.65-0.70 (tied bottom block). ONLY at equal optimizer/lr/T use architecture: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.8-0.9); plain+more-LN beats residual+fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5 (25/29), residual leads at Δ<0.03 (14/24); 0-LN residual wins only at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Deeper wins XOR (26-11). Best CE: 1 turn 1e-3-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.5, 3 turns ~0.6. 1-turn at Δ≥0.5 = confidence-tail regime (coupled-wd exception, K1046).

Optimizer conversion for the Δ rule (K1001). Adagrad: steps decay ~lr/√t, so it equals Adam only at ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger lr — same arch, lr ratio ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70, 10× coin flip, ≥30× Adagrad 9/9; within Adagrad larger lr wins 40/41 (3e-3 never too big); Adagrad lr≤1e-4 is frozen. SGD: plain (m=0) lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins 3/141 pairs vs a >15× larger adaptive Δ; LM CE stays ≈ln V). SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10 on classification (131/146), lr/3 on MSE regression (59/71; beats Adagrad ≤1e-3 and Adam ≤1e-4), lr/30 on bigram LM (68/70; beats Adam-family 1/18). These credits assume ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less (K1038).

Tabular classification depth/LN rule (1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ in core-rule units, NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad). Shared Δ<0.1: normal rule — more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17, strongest on smooth_additive (deeper 24-8; q_1a7ca0 2-block 2-LN beat 1-block wide 1-LN), absent on piecewise_boundary (5-6) and sparse_interaction (6-3): there pick most-LN regardless of depth. Shared Δ≥0.1: boundary already learned, CE set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider GELU/SiLU nets with fewer LN: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. Picks 26/32 arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse (XOR ≤4 features: deeper 15-4).

Depth × residual × task (MLPs, same optimizer). MSE regression: depth helps even without residuals — deeper residual beats shallower plain 32-2, deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15, deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 at lr·T<0.1); equal-depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets amplify the depth edge; deep plain stacks with 0 LN are the exception (signal attenuation). Classification (CE): depth WITHOUT residual hurts — shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13, deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14 (exceptions: spiral plain with more LN, K1041; tabular Δ≥0.1 reverses depth, K1043).

Tabular LONG budget (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): optimum Δ≈0.03-0.3; Δ≥0.5 (Adam-family lr≥1e-3 at T≥512) loses — lab smooth_additive Δ0.03-0.15 beats Δ0.5-1.5 8/8 (CE ratio 1.47), sparse 6/6; dataflip 4/4 (q_86f129, q_565490, q_e79cfd, q_f05f74 RMSprop 1e-4 + LN beat Adam 1e-3); q_b070ff AdamW 1e-3×2048 (Δ2) last, Adagrad 3e-3 3-LN residual (Δ0.27) first. Δ<0.03 still loses to Δ0.03-0.15 (6/6). Depth reverses early: shallow 2-block wide beats 4-block already at Δ0.03-0.1 (16/16, ratio 0.59-0.75; q_eeb76a); among shallow more LN wins, among deep residual > plain. At 4 epochs see K1021.

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (higher wd 3-10, all within 1%), Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas 5-5, β2 0.95 vs 0.999 ~even (7-4). Never let them override a Δ gap; order near-twins by architecture. EXCEPTION — CE→1e-4 regime (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family Δ≥0.5): torch Adam with COUPLED weight_decay≥1e-4 loses to its AdamW or wd=0 twin (lab+controlled 36/36; CE ratio ~10× at wd 1e-4, 56× at 1e-3, 800× at 1e-2; q_6a81f1) and at T=2048 even to AdamW 3e-5 β2 0.95 (Δ0.06; q_65d623; controlled 2/2, but not at T=1024). AdamW at the same lr ≈ wd=0. Not seen on bigram LM.

CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1049), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging) is noisy and worsens with T: vs rivals with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins 22/36 corpus; on univariate at T≥1024 it LOSES (lab 1/10, median MSE ratio 6.3; controlled −2.5cos(2πx)·x: 0.014 vs Adagrad 1e-3 0.0011, Adam 3e-3 0.0015; q_c1fb6a Adagrad 1e-3 won) — rank it below Adam 3e-3, RMSprop 1e-3 and Adagrad ≥1e-3; at T=512 it wins 18/23, at T=256 ~half. Adam 3e-3 is safe (wins 84%). (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam-family lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4; GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 safe.

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4; q_c197cb 0.999 won). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. Only exception: two-spiral with Adam-family lr≥1e-3, where coupled Adam weight_decay≥1e-3 loses big (K1040).

MLP architecture default (same optimizer/lr/T; regression, XOR, tabular Δ<0.1; spiral: K1020): score = #LayerNorm'd blocks + 1 if residual; pick the highest (92/128 arch-only winners; plain with ≥2 more LN beats residual: lab 100/143, corpus 17/19). TIE plain(+1 LN) vs residual: at Δ<0.1 a plain net with ≤3 blocks wins 61/76; a deep (≥4) plain net is a toss-up (32/68); at Δ≥0.1 lean residual (30/49). Other ties: regression activation ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last LN (K1022), then depth. Exceptions: shared-SGD regression K1039; XOR ≥8 features Δ≥0.05 K1018; tabular Δ≥0.1 → shallow/less-LN overconfidence rule.

Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets. Activation is a tie-break AFTER LN count/residual (K1006). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1047) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss sits on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied (order them by architecture: K1006/K1020); a 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes in 256-512 steps; deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11). Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly everything stuck → pick the largest Δ).

Bigram LM, GRU vs transformer (same optimizer): a GRU LM beats a post-LN causal transformer in 20/21 same-optimizer pairs (corpus 16/17 at equal lr/T), at weak and strong Δ — rank the GRU first; at Δ<0.02 (e.g. RMSprop 3e-5×256, q_192d8f) it wins outright because every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU starts nearest it. Mechanism: the task is a first-order lookup P(y|x_t); the GRU maps the current token straight to its output and its tanh-bounded state gives near-uniform initial logits, while post-LN transformers start ~0.1-0.2 nats above ln V and must learn to ignore attention mixing. Transformer-vs-transformer shape: K1017.

Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue, Δ<0.1): deeper-is-better is strong for smooth/compositional targets — tabular smooth_additive (deeper 24-8), XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4), oscillatory univariate targets — but weak when the rule is piecewise_boundary (5-6) or sparse_interaction (6-3) or XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7): there prefer the most-LN candidate regardless of depth (XOR ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05: K1018). Polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.

SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1049 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).

Spiral coupled weight decay — applies ONLY to two-spiral CE (1-1.5 turns) with Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024 (CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than an AdamW or wd=0 twin at the same lr (controlled 12/12 cells, CE ratio 0.002-0.03; q_6a81f1). It does NOT make AdamW better in general, and it never overrides a Δ gap (K1001) or applies at wd≤1e-4 or lr≤3e-4. β2 flips with lr here: weak tie-break only.

Synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features) with shared Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ, not raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad): the boundary is learned and test CE is set by overconfidence. (i) Architecture reverses: prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets, GELU/SiLU, fewer LN (shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16; picks 26/32 arch-only winners). (ii) Extra Δ hurts: once the smaller Δ≥0.1, a ≥3× larger Δ wins only 63/146 (sparse_interaction 5/33, CE ratio 1.44; smooth_additive 22/55; piecewise 36/58) — target Δ≈0.1-0.3. Δ<0.1: normal rules (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17, larger Δ wins 59-95%). XOR/spiral do not reverse; 32 epochs: tabular LONG-budget rule.

Tabular LONG budget (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs) overfits early. (i) smooth_additive: the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices with ≥1 LN (dataflip 3/3: q_86f129, q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, q_e79cfd; controlled CE 0.43 vs 0.26-0.33); piecewise/sparse_interaction: larger Δ still usually wins (10/12) unless Δ≥3. (ii) Depth: shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block ones already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (controlled 16/16, CE ratio 0.59-0.75; q_eeb76a); among shallow nets more LN wins, among deep residual > plain. At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) neither holds.

SGD conversion for the Δ rule (K1001; fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs): Δ_SGD = lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with |g|≈0.01 for classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression, 0.03 for MSE regression with momentum 0.9 (SGD m0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3; 59/71), 0.003 for bigram LM (≈ Adam at lr/30; SGD m0.9 beat adaptive in 1/18 LM pairs). So plain SGD lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8%; 3/141 when adaptive Δ >15× larger); SGD m0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 is a real contender (beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam ≤1e-4, unstable RMSprop 3e-3), but m0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam at the same lr. Full credit needs ≥1 LayerNorm in the SGD net (K1038).

Depth × residual × task (MLPs, same optimizer/lr/T). REGRESSION (MSE): depth helps even without residuals — deeper residual beats shallower plain 32-2, deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15, deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32; oscillatory/composite targets (sin(2πx), cos(2π sin…)) amplify it; only deep plain stacks with 0 LN usually lose. CLASSIFICATION (CE): depth WITHOUT residual hurts — shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13 while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14 (deep residual wins 53% of appearances vs 29% deep plain). Width at equal depth: coin flip on regression (5-5). Tabular Δ≥0.1 or 32 epochs reverse to shallow.

Two-spiral WIDTH (exception to K1016 'capacity is not the bottleneck'): at equal LN count, residual flag and optimizer, the WIDER MLP wins — width-only pairs lab+corpus 9/9 (median CE ratio ~0.89; plain SGD, Adagrad, Adam) and controlled one-turn spiral 6/6 at small and large Δ (plain SGD 3e-3×256: CE 0.51/0.41/0.30 at width 32/64/128; Adam 1e-3×256: 0.095/0.035/0.011). Wider-but-shallower at equal LN: corpus 3/4, q_0a7f2f (w96 depth-1 beat w48 depth-3). Apply after LN count (K1020), before depth. XOR/regression: width ~coin flip.

SGD (all families; compute Δ with momentum + K1019 calibration). MSE REGRESSION EXCEPTION FIRST: a plain-SGD (m=0) net with ≥1 LayerNorm is NOT frozen — it beats adaptive rivals with 1-4× its calibrated Δ 70/102 (lab; q_645b86 LN SGD beat 0-LN RMSprop 1e-4) and 0-LN adaptive rivals at 4-30× 13/21; vs LN'd rivals at ≥4× it loses (32/147). Elsewhere (LMs, classification, 0-LN nets) plain SGD lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8%; LM CE stays ≈ln V). SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at ~lr/10: lr 1e-3-3e-3 beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3, but at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr. Bigram LM: SGD weaker (≈Adam lr/30).

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss sits on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied (order that bottom block by architecture, K1012). Deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11; ≥8-feature exception K1018). Spiral CE scale by turns: 1 turn best ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly all stuck → pick largest Δ). Spiral architecture: LN count/residual by optimizer in K1020, depth in K1052.

Bigram LM GRU vs post-LN transformer: compare Δ (K1001) FIRST, architecture second. Transformer Δ ≥1.25× the GRU's: transformer wins (corpus 9/9, lab 30/32; q_b6c184 AdamW 3e-4 beat GRU Adam 1e-4) — EXCEPT a transformer at Adam-family lr≥1e-3 vs a GRU with Δ≥0.01: GRU wins 14/19 (overshoot, K1004b; q_3327a7). GRU Δ ≥1.25× larger: GRU 46/48. Same optimizer+lr+T: GRU beats transformers with d_model≤64 (corpus 18/19, lab 12/18; miss q_b6a00f, 2-layer GRU last at RMSprop 1e-4×512) but loses to d_model-128 ones at 0.02≤Δ<0.1 (lab 13/14). All Δ<0.02 (CE≈ln V): GRU wins ties (q_96d06a). Cross-optimizer parity (0.8-1.25×): transformer 7/11.

Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on XOR/tabular classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13 corpus; lab tabular 18/31, XOR 9/13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So on XOR/tabular CE never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; TWO-SPIRAL is the exception: a deeper plain net at equal width with LN on most blocks wins (K1052). For MSE a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T) flips with Δ (core-rule units). Δ<0.1: WIDER wins — larger d_ff at equal d_model/layers (corpus 3/3, lab 12/13; q_b6a00f d_ff 256<128<64 in CE) and larger d_model (15/15 at 0.02-0.1); fewest layers wins 21/21 at 0.02≤Δ<0.1, but at Δ<0.02 (all ≈ln V) deeper wins 10/17. 0.1≤Δ<0.5: weak (fewer layers 10/17, smaller d_model 9/13, wider d_ff 2/5). Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model 5/6, narrower d_ff 4/5, fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (K1004b). Across optimizers at Δ parity (<1.5×), a 4× d_ff edge beats the optimizer gap (q_9c878f).

Two-spiral MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): with ADAPTIVE optimizers score LN count FIRST, residual as tie-break; with SGD put residual FIRST. Δ in K1001 units (SGD lr·T·0.01/(1−m): plain SGD 1e-3×1024 = 0.01, not 1.0). Same residual status: more LN wins (lab 163/206). Plain-more-LN vs residual-fewer-LN: adaptive 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 52/62 lab; Δ<0.03 split (lab plain 20/24, corpus residual 5/5); Δ≥0.5 6/10. SGD: residual wins 7/7 lab + q_33377e (2.5 turns: residual 3-LN, 2-LN beat plain 4-LN). Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain ≥1 LN at Δ<0.5 (8/59), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03 (q_343ea5), coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).

Two-spiral DEPTH exception to 'deep plain loses on CE' (K1015): at the SAME width and activation, a deeper PLAIN MLP with ≥2 more blocks and LN on most blocks beats a shallower residual MLP (same optimizer; lab 33/40 matched width/act, median CE ratio 0.85; gap ≥2 38/50; controlled 1-turn Adam 1e-3×256 d4-plain all-LN vs d2-residual ratio 0.33; q_f66110 4-block plain ReLU+LN beat 3-block 0-LN residual). Fails if the deep net is narrower, has only 1 LN (controlled ratio 2.2), depth gap=1 (2/5), or 1-turn Δ<0.03 (0/5); the corpus misses (1/8) all violate these. A deep residual LN net beats both. Winner pick still: LN count first (K1020); 'depth+LN' scoring is worse (7/27 lab).

Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2. EXCEPTION — MSE regression vs Adam 3e-3 with ≥2 LN and T≥512: Adagrad lr≥3e-4 wins (17/17; K1054).

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (27/37). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier with ≥1 LN beats SiLU with 1 more LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples) on smooth_additive, where Δ 0.01-0.15 beats Δ≥0.5 (long-budget rule K1053). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1009). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).

SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): a ReLU/LeakyReLU net that HAS ≥1 LayerNorm beats a SiLU/GELU net with equal or one MORE LN (equal LN: corpus 9/10, lab 15/18; one fewer LN: corpus 2/2, lab 7/7, controlled 6/6; MSE ratio 0.04-0.5). But a rectifier net with ZERO LN usually loses to a smooth net with ≥1 LN (rectifier wins only corpus 3/7, lab 6/18; q_6ebcfd: 4-layer SiLU with 1 LN beat 1-layer 0-LN LeakyReLU) — 0-LN SGD nets are near-frozen (K1038). Smooth net with ≥2 more LN: toss-up, keep LN count first (K1006). Under Adam-family keep K1006.

Tabular LONG budget (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, total_samples_seen=32768 ≈32 epochs, any steps×batch): test CE is overfit-limited. On smooth_additive the high-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to a Δ≈0.01-0.15 choice with ≥1 LN, even SGD m0.9 3e-4, AdamW 3e-5 or RMSprop 1e-4 (dataflip 6/6: q_565490, q_e79cfd, q_f05f74, q_86f129, q_38d93d, q_b0b41d). Depth: at Δ 0.03-0.15 shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-5 block nets (controlled 16/16, corpus 2/2, CE ratio 0.6-0.75); at Δ<0.03 deep residual+LN is fine (corpus shallow 2/5; q_38d93d 5-block SGD won). Piecewise/sparse: larger Δ usually still wins (10/12) unless Δ≥3. At 4 epochs none of this holds.

Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW lr=3e-3 on MSE REGRESSION (same architecture, 256 rows, bs16-64): if the net has ≥2 LayerNorm blocks and T≥512, Adagrad lr 3e-4-3e-3 BEATS Adam 3e-3 despite 10-100× smaller Δ — exception to K1001/K1002/K1004 (≥2 LN, T≥512: corpus 2/2 q_3d7396, q_9e733e; q_6e1a99 x**4 T=1024 4-layer 3-LN ReLU; lab+controlled 17/17 total; median MSE ratio 0.02-0.13). With <2 LN, Adagrad 3e-4 loses (0/7) but Adagrad ≥1e-3 wins 5/5 at T≥512. At T=256 Adam 3e-3 wins (8/8). Applies only vs Adam lr 3e-3; vs Adam ≤1e-3 untested in this regime (Adam 1e-3 won 6/6 corpus pairs elsewhere). Mostly univariate.

RMSprop on MSE REGRESSION (exception to the Δ rule): (a) lr≥1e-3: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ, RMSprop 3e-3 wins only 22/36 corpus pairs (1e-3 univariate 1/4); it wins 6/6 only when its MLP is clearly better (more LN + residual, e.g. q_65db92). (b) UNIVARIATE regression, any lr: at EQUAL lr Adam/AdamW beats RMSprop (lab 16/18 same-net pairs; controlled 6/6 at lr≥1e-4, MSE ratio 17-550×); vs Adam with 1-3× smaller Δ RMSprop still wins only 16/39. Multivariate at lr≤3e-4: RMSprop ≈ Adam (5/6). Adam 3e-3 on regression is safe (loses 2/35); MLP classification lr 3e-3 safe. LM lr ceiling: see bigram optimizer rule (d_model=128).

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual (tabular: +1 more if last block has LN, K1022); pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then later last-LN, then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: a ≥1-LN rectifier beats SiLU/GELU with 1 more LN (K1039); SPIRAL: K1020; XOR: residual bonus weak (K1010), ≥8 feat Δ≥0.05: K1018; tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70, near-tied (order those by architecture). Among equal optimizers more LN helps (spiral 20-5; XOR ≤4 features corpus 7/7, lab 10/12) and on XOR ≤4 features deeper wins, but a RESIDUAL bonus is NOT reliable on XOR (residual vs plain at equal LN: lab 6/10, equal depth 3/6): q_ae7f73 (4 feat, AdamW 3e-4×256) plain 3-block GELU beat residual 3-block GELU, and 1-block residual LeakyReLU was last. Spiral: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (pick largest Δ).

Bigram LM optimizer/learning rate. FIRST the lr cap: a post-LN transformer LM with d_model=128 under Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 loses to an adaptive lr 1e-4–3e-4 rival at ANY T, even T=256 (corpus+lab+dataflip 1/11; q_78c004: same 1-layer d128 net, Adam 1e-4×256 (Δ0.026) beat RMSprop 1e-3 (Δ0.26)). At d_model 32-64 lr≥1e-3 is a coin flip (16/29); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). Otherwise labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V: among choices with Δ≥0.1 prefer Δ nearest ~0.3 (picks 52/66 winners vs 47/66 for max-Δ); Δ≥1 is likely overshoot; below Δ≈0.1 max-Δ applies. All Δ<0.02: every LM ≈ln V, GRU wins ties.

LN PLACEMENT (MLP pre-LN blocks). Synthetic TABULAR classification with Δ<0.1: a LayerNorm on the LAST hidden block (right before the head) counts as one extra LN — score = LN count + residual + 1 if last block has LN: corpus pairwise 46/49 vs 38/44 without the bonus; lab 150/228 (same 66% rate, 26 more pairs decided). Multivariate regression and spiral: use last-LN only as a TIE-BREAKER at equal LN count and residual status (corpus 11/12, median loss ratio ~0.80); as a +1 bonus it hurts there (lab 71% vs 77%). Univariate regression and XOR: ignore placement (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4). Tabular Δ≥0.1: use the tabular reversal rules instead.

Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 16 features, total_samples_seen≥16384, i.e. ≥16 epochs): on smooth_additive ANY choice with Δ≥0.5 (Adam-family lr·T≥0.5, e.g. Adam 3e-4×2048 or 1e-3×512) LOSES to a Δ≈0.01-0.15 rival (Adagrad 1e-3×2048 Δ≈0.09, Adam 3e-5-1e-4, SGD 1e-3 + LN): lab 13/16 pairs in 7 sets (CE ratio ≈0.9), with or without LN on the small-Δ net (0-LN 4/5); dataflip 4/4 (q_86f129, q_565490, q_e79cfd, q_f6b7e9: Adagrad 1e-3 1-block 0-LN beat Adam 3e-4 2-block). Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction: larger Δ usually wins (corpus 6/8, dataflip 4/4) unless Δ≥3.

SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit — but only if the rectifier net itself has ≥1 LN (corpus+lab 9/9). A 0-LN rectifier net vs a 1-LN smooth net loses 6/8 (q_60f231: 5-block plain GELU with one middle LN beat 1-block 0-LN LeakyReLU; cf. K1038). Rectifier vs smooth at equal LN: corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).

Adagrad conversion (any family): Adagrad's step decays ~lr/√t, so its Δ=2·lr·√T equals Adam-family Δ at lr_eq=2·lr/√T: Adagrad ≈ Adam at lr/8 (T=256), lr/11 (512), lr/16 (1024), lr/23 (2048). Compare Δ, not lr ratio. Adagrad/Adam Δ ratio <0.5 → Adam wins 171/186 corpus pairs; 0.5-1 → Adam 7/10; 1-1.3 → Adagrad 11/11 (10× lr at T=256: corpus 8/8, lab same-net 14/17 but tiny margin ~2%, so architecture can override; 10× at T≥512: Adam 7/9); >1.3 → Adagrad 28/32. Within Adagrad larger lr wins 40/41. Adagrad lr≤1e-4 is near-frozen vs adaptive rivals, but vs plain SGD compute both Δs (q_b33e04: residual Adagrad 1e-4×512 beat plain SGD 1e-3 at Δ parity).

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then last LN nearest the head (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17, 14/20). Exceptions: PLAIN nets under SGD at Δ<0.03: an un-normed LAST block voids extra LNs (K1022); shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: K1020; XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.03: K1018; tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss sits on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70, near-tied. At equal optimizer, LN count (not depth or residual) drives wins (corpus): deeper wins when it also has more LN (XOR 20/24, spiral 12/18) but only 6/16 at equal LN; residual beats plain at equal LN (XOR 5/6, spiral 4/7) yet loses on XOR when it has fewer LN (2/8). Plain-net LN placement: K1022; XOR ≥8 features at Δ≥0.03: K1018. Spiral difficulty: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (pick largest Δ).

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.03, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05, Adagrad 1e-3×256): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOWER beats deeper: depth gap ≥3 corpus 2/3 + lab 4/4 (CE ratio 0.5-0.64); gap 1-2 lab 23/28 (ratio 0.79), corpus 3/7 — lean shallow (q_c010e1: 1-block w64 > 2-block > 3-5 blocks; q_b11fea: 3-block GELU first, 5-block last; q_bfba99: all 2-block nets beat both 5-block residual nets). With ≤4 features keep deeper (lab shallower 1/16 at Δ 0.03-0.1). For Δ<0.03 the LN rules hold for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).

LN PLACEMENT (pre-LN MLPs, same optimizer/lr/T): k_trail = unnormalized hidden blocks after the LAST LayerNorm'd block. PLAIN (non-residual) nets trained with SGD (plain or m=0.9) at Δ<0.03: placement beats LN count — smaller k_trail wins at equal LN (lab 9/9, corpus 2/2, ratio 0.75) AND with 1-2 fewer LN (lab 14/15; controlled 3/3 on tabular, 8-feat XOR, oscillatory MSE, ratio ~0.7); q_e63c16: 4-LN net ending in an un-normed block ranked last behind 1-LN nets. Adagrad: same direction (equal LN 4/4). Adam-family: only a weak tie-break (16/24, ratio 0.96) — keep LN count first (fewer-but-late 1/6). Residual nets: effect vanishes/reverses (controlled 0/6). Spiral or Δ≥0.03: ignore.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1; same optimizer): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then WIDER/shallower, NOT deeper (equal-LN deeper-narrower loses 24/33, K1056). Picks ~94/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN 27/37. Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU with 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: K1020; XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: K1018; tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T), the boundary is learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers) wider nets with GELU/SiLU (shallower wins corpus 21-5, lab 42-15; smooth act. 16/16, lab 38-11) and 1 rather than several LN (17-6), BUT never credit ZERO LN: a 0-LN net beats a ≥1-LN rival only corpus 2/6, lab 17/37 (q_37a3e5: 1-LN residual LeakyReLU beat 0-LN plain SiLU). When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693; same optimizer/lr/T). Near-frozen Δ≲0.01: all choices sit at CE 0.63-0.70 with 1-5% gaps; order by LN COUNT (more-LN wins lab XOR 76/112, spiral 43/67; controlled XOR Adagrad 1e-4×256: all-LN 4-layer 0.632 vs 0.655-0.687), NOT by residual (XOR 34/71, coin flip). At Δ 0.03-0.1: more LN wins spiral 189/233 (CE ratio 0.87), XOR 38/53; deeper wins spiral 117/148 but XOR only 30/50 (≥8 features: shallow-wide, K1018); residual is no advantage (spiral 72/173). Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly all stuck → pick largest Δ).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T). FIRST compute core-rule Δ (Adagrad Δ=2·lr·√T: 1e-4×256 → 0.003, not lr·T). EQUAL d_model: Δ<0.02 (near-frozen, CE≈ln V) → DEEPER wins 19/28 (q_96d1aa: 2-layer beat 1-layer, Adagrad 1e-4×256); 0.02-0.1 coin flip 8/15; 0.1≤Δ<0.5 → fewer layers wins 23/23 (q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a ~1-2% CE tie-break — wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger d_model wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 (Adam/RMSprop 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512) smaller d_model wins 5/6 (q_528b22, q_17f213): order by d_model ascending, then layers. GRU vs transformer: K1011.

Two-spiral classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual only as tie-break (K1006 sum). Same residual status: more LN wins at every Δ (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-with-more-LN vs residual-with-fewer-LN: 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 25/29 (lab 16/18, controlled 6/6; q_31abed, q_9c257e); Δ<0.03 near coin flip (residual 14/24); Δ≥0.5 mixed (residual lab 5/6, controlled 1/4). Residual with ZERO LN ranks LAST at every Δ: vs plain ≥1-LN lab 8/59 at Δ<0.5; at Δ≥0.5 lab 4/6 but controlled AdamW 1e-3×1024 it was last of 5 at 1 AND 2 turns, behind even a plain 0-LN net (q_b9a1d3; CE 1.9-2.8×). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03, coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).

Synthetic TABULAR classification, both choices at core-rule Δ≥0.1 (Adam 1e-3×256 or 1e-4×1024; Adagrad 2·lr·√T): more Δ stops helping. A ≥3× larger Δ LOSES: sparse_interaction wins 5/33 (CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55, piecewise 36/58. Within ≤3.5× Δ is irrelevant (larger wins lab 77/172): decide by architecture — a net with LN/residual beats a 0-LN/plain one 57/82 (ratio 0.83; q_37a3e5: AdamW 3e-4 1-LN residual beat RMSprop 1e-4 0-LN plain SiLU), then shape (K1009). If the smaller Δ is 0.03-0.1, larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs, but not at 32 epochs on smooth_additive (K1032).

UNIVARIATE regression, WIDE multi-layer MLP (width≥128, depth≥2), choices differ in optimizer/lr: lr·T≥1 OVERSHOOTS — prefer a choice with Δ≈0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3) over Adam/AdamW/RMSprop at Δ≥1. Corpus optimizer-only 5/5 (q_3d7396, q_9e733e); lab same-arch Δ≥1 wins only 9/59 (MSE ratio 6.4); controlled w128-256 11/12. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and loses (q_f609cc; lab 3/7) unless the high side has Δ≥5. NOT for 1-layer nets (Δ≥1 wins same-arch 13/13, ratio 0.03) nor multivariate (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10); narrow (≤96) multi-layer nets are a coin flip (same-arch 24/43; controlled w64: sin target best at Δ0.5, x³ at Δ1.5).

Depth × residual × LN (MLPs, same optimizer). REGRESSION: depth pays only via the LN/residual it brings — deeper-narrower with MORE LN beats shallower-wider 151/197 (MSE ratio 0.60), but at EQUAL LN count and residual status deeper-narrower LOSES 24/33 (ratio 1.12; q_fbd6d4: 1-layer w48 beat 2-layer w24, both 0-LN residual); shallower-residual beats deeper-narrower-plain at equal LN 12/15; at equal width deeper wins 13/18. Oscillatory targets amplify the gain from 4-5 normalized residual blocks. CLASSIFICATION (XOR/spiral/tabular): deeper residual beats shallower plain 170/247 (ratio 0.84-0.94); deeper plain vs shallower residual is a coin flip (138/262).

Bigram LM Δ ceiling depends on MODEL TYPE (same model+set, Δ per K1001, lab 10-seed, mostly T=256). TRANSFORMER: a bigger Δ helps only while it stays <0.1 (6/6). Once it reaches ≥0.1 it loses to Δ<0.03 in 7/11 pairs. Δ≥0.3 loses to Δ 0.1-0.3 in 14/14, and Δ≥1 loses to any Δ≥0.03 in 11/11 (CE +2-20%). Deep (≥3-layer) transformers with weak signal (alpha 0.8) can prefer Δ≈0.01 (q_6148e3: RMSprop 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3 at T=256). GRU: max-Δ holds through Δ<1 (44/44 pairs whose smaller Δ<0.1, CE ratio ~0.95); Δ≥0.3 vs 0.1-0.3 is a wash (1/5). Corpus: picking Δ nearest 0.3 wins 52/66 bigram questions. If every Δ<0.02, all LMs stay ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.
